doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop, band changes and the road
title: Not knowing Ornette's scene; leaving LA in 1947 and working 48 weeks a year
summary: Hamilton did not know Ornette Coleman, Don Cherry or Blackwell in LA since he left in 1947; the quintet then worked 48 weeks a year with long club runs in Ohio, and he once played in Mercer Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well we can talk about Ornette.
Ornette, no I didn’t know him before he came east.
Okay, so you didn’t see him on the scene. He wasn’t on the scene in LA?
No, no, not when I was there.
How about Blackwell, how about when Blackwell came?
No? That was a little after I guess.
You know, I virtually in a sense left LA in ‘47 when I came east with Lena, you know, and I was -­

Well my quintet was in ‘55, you know, but we were in LA for about, what eight or nine months and then boom, we hit the road. Hit the road Jack. Do you know, man in those days, I stayed on the road -- we worked at least 48 weeks a year, out of the year. I mean that.
You only had a month off then.

And I’d take off during Thanksgiving and I wouldn’t go back to work until the first of the year. I never played New Year’s Eve. It was like during that period -- for instance you take Ohio, you could play Ohio man, you could stay in Ohio almost two years because at that time all the joints, man you were booked for four or five weeks at a run, you know. It was no one night or two nights and things like that. You stayed in a joint two or three weeks at a time, you dig? And like I said man, you could stay in Ohio. Between Cleveland, Cincinnati, you know, you name them, you could stay in Ohio, which I did, which we could, a long time. As a matter of fact man, when I joined Mercer Ellington’s band, he was headquartered out of Columbus. You didn’t know I played with Mercer, right?
I was going to ask you, what year was that? For how long?

Well not too long because I was with Lena at the time and we were off and they needed a drummer, and Luther and Mercer were boon coons, you know, so I went out there. Hell man, when I was in the service, man I played with King Colax. I played with Nat Toles. I took off -- I played with all them junk bands, you know.
